spec.goal: Add a read route GET /items/:id to the toy items API. When :id is a canonical decimal integer that names an item in the in-memory store, respond 200 with that item serialized as JSON ({ id, name }) — deep-equal to the object POST /items returned for it. In every other case — a well-formed integer id with no matching item, or an id that is not a canonical decimal integer (e.g. "abc", "1.5", "-1", " 1") — respond 404 with the JSON body { "error": "not found" }. No other route's behavior, response shape, or status code changes, and the store stays in-memory and per-app-instance.

acceptance.given: A fresh app instance where POST /items {"name":"widget"} has returned 201 with body {"id":1,"name":"widget"}
acceptance.then: The response status is 200, the content-type is application/json, and the parsed body deep-equals the exact object returned by the POST ({"id":1,"name":"widget"}) with no extra or missing keys

acceptance.given: A fresh app instance with no items created
acceptance.then: The response status is 404, the content-type is application/json, and the parsed body deep-equals {"error":"not found"}

acceptance.given: A fresh app instance where exactly one item has been created and has id 1
acceptance.when: A client sends GET /items/999 (a well-formed integer id no item holds)
acceptance.then: The response status is 404 and the parsed body deep-equals {"error":"not found"}

acceptance.given: A fresh app instance where an item with id 1 exists
acceptance.then: The response status is 404 and the parsed body deep-equals {"error":"not found"} — the same status and body as the missing-item case, with no 500 and no stack trace in the body

acceptance.given: A fresh app instance where an item with id 1 exists
acceptance.when: A client sends GET /items/1.5, GET /items/-1, GET /items/1e0, GET /items/%201 (URL-encoded leading space) and GET /items/0x1 in turn
acceptance.then: Each response has status 404 and a body deep-equal to {"error":"not found"}; none of them returns the item with id 1

acceptance.given: A fresh app instance where POST /items has created items named "a", "b" and "c", receiving ids 1, 2 and 3
acceptance.when: A client sends GET /items/1, GET /items/2 and GET /items/3
acceptance.then: Each response is 200 and returns exactly its own item — {"id":1,"name":"a"}, {"id":2,"name":"b"} and {"id":3,"name":"c"} respectively — with no cross-contamination between ids

acceptance.given: Two separate app instances created by createApp(), where an item with id 1 was created only on the first
acceptance.when: A client sends GET /items/1 to the second instance
acceptance.then: The response status is 404 with body {"error":"not found"}, proving the store is still per-instance and no module-level state leaked

acceptance.given: A fresh app instance with the new route registered
acceptance.when: A client sends GET /items (the collection route) both before and after creating one item
acceptance.then: The responses are unchanged from current behavior: 200 with [] before, and 200 with an array containing exactly the created item after — the :id route does not shadow or alter the collection route

acceptance.given: A fresh app instance with the new route registered
acceptance.when: The pre-existing suites toy/test/items.test.js and toy/test/health.test.js are run
acceptance.then: Every pre-existing test still passes unmodified: GET /health returns 200 {"status":"ok"}, POST /items with a name returns 201, and POST /items with a missing name returns 400 {"error":"name is required"}

acceptance.when: `npm test` is run from the toy/ directory
acceptance.then: The command exits 0 and the run includes new tests covering the 200 hit, the missing-id 404 and the non-integer-id 404

touched_surfaces.ref: createApp (toy/src/app.js) — route registration order and the in-memory items Map lookup

out_of_scope: POST /items name-length validation and the 400 {"error":"name too long"} body — that is work item wi-2
GET /health uptime_seconds — that is work item wi-3
Any write or mutation route for a single item: PUT, PATCH or DELETE /items/:id
Persistence of any kind — the store stays an in-memory Map that resets per createApp() instance
Changing the id allocation scheme (nextId stays a monotonic integer counter) or supporting UUID/string/slug ids
Pagination, filtering, sorting or query parameters on GET /items or GET /items/:id
Authentication, authorization, rate limiting and CORS
Changing the error body shape, status codes or messages of any existing route, including the POST /items missing-name 400
405 Method Not Allowed handling, HEAD/OPTIONS semantics, and a global 404 handler for unknown paths outside /items/:id
Response headers beyond what express res.json() already sets (no ETag, Cache-Control or Location work)
Structured logging, metrics or tracing for the new route
Changes to toy/src/server.js, toy/package.json, the test harness toy/test/helpers.js, or anything outside the toy/ directory
risk_reasons: Read-only GET endpoint with no mutations or side effects
Existing routes and behaviors remain unchanged with explicit test coverage
No data schema modifications—reuses existing item structure
No infrastructure, persistence, or external service changes
Changes isolated to single route file and test file
Easily reversible with zero lasting impact
No involvement of auth, payments, or critical systems

tasks.description: Implement the GET /items/:id route handler. Validate that :id is a canonical decimal integer (reject 1.5, -1, 1e0, %201, 0x1, abc, etc.), look it up in the in-memory store, and respond with 200 and the item JSON {id, name} if found, or 404 with {"error": "not found"} otherwise.

owned_surfaces.ref: createApp (toy/src/app.js) — route registration order and the in-memory items Map lookup

tasks.description: Write test cases for GET /items/:id covering: successful retrieval of an existing item (200), missing items returning 404, and invalid ID formats (non-integers, non-canonical integers) also returning 404. Verify that all pre-existing tests in items.test.js and health.test.js continue to pass without modification.

spec.goal: POST /items rejects a name longer than 64 characters with HTTP 400 and body { "error": "name too long" }, while accepting a name of exactly 64 characters with the existing 201 create behavior. "Longer than 64" is measured as JavaScript String.length (UTF-16 code units) on the raw request value, with no trimming or normalization. The length check runs only after the existing presence/type check in toy/src/app.js, so the current missing-name / non-string / empty-string 400 { "error": "name is required" } responses are unchanged. No other route, field, or response shape changes.

acceptance.given: a running app instance with an empty item store
acceptance.when: a client sends POST /items with content-type application/json and body { "name": <a 65-character string> }
acceptance.then: the response status is 400, the JSON body deep-equals { "error": "name too long" }, and a subsequent GET /items returns [] (the item was not created)

acceptance.given: a running app instance with an empty item store
acceptance.when: a client sends POST /items with body { "name": <a string of exactly 64 characters> }
acceptance.then: the response status is 201, the JSON body is { id: <number>, name: <the same 64-character string> }, and a subsequent GET /items returns exactly that one item

acceptance.given: a running app instance with an empty item store
acceptance.when: a client sends POST /items with body { "name": <a string of exactly 63 characters> }
acceptance.then: the response status is 201 and the created item's name equals the 63-character string, confirming the boundary rejects only lengths strictly greater than 64

acceptance.when: a client sends POST /items with body {} (no name field)
acceptance.then: the response status is 400 and the JSON body deep-equals { "error": "name is required" }, unchanged from current behavior

acceptance.when: a client sends POST /items with body { "name": "" } (empty string) and, separately, { "name": 123 } (non-string)
acceptance.then: in both cases the response status is 400 and the JSON body deep-equals { "error": "name is required" }; the new length check never turns these into "name too long"

acceptance.given: a running app instance with an empty item store and a name of 200 characters (well past the limit)
acceptance.when: a client sends POST /items with that 200-character name and then sends POST /items with { "name": "widget" }
acceptance.then: the first response is 400 { "error": "name too long" }, the second is 201, and the created item's id is 1 — a rejected over-length request consumes no id and mutates no state

acceptance.when: `npm test` is run from the toy/ directory
acceptance.then: every pre-existing test in toy/test/items.test.js and toy/test/health.test.js still passes alongside the new length-limit tests, and the run exits 0

out_of_scope: Any change to GET /items, GET /health, or GET /items/:id (the latter belongs to wi-1 — do not add or modify that route here).
Changing the existing missing-name / non-string / empty-string error message, status, or check ordering; 'name is required' stays exactly as it is and is still evaluated first.
Trimming, whitespace collapsing, Unicode normalization (NFC/NFD), grapheme-cluster counting, or byte-length counting — the limit is raw String.length in UTF-16 code units.
Making the 64-character limit configurable via env var, config file, or request parameter; the constant is hard-coded in toy/src/app.js.
Adding a minimum-length rule, character-set validation, content/profanity filtering, or duplicate-name rejection.
Validating or limiting any field other than `name`, and rejecting requests that carry extra unknown fields.
Introducing a validation library (zod, joi, express-validator) or a shared validation middleware layer; the check stays inline in the existing route handler.
Changing the error response envelope shape (e.g. adding `code`, `field`, or `details` keys) for this or any other error.
Truncating an over-length name and accepting it instead of rejecting it.
Request body size limits, rate limiting, auth, or any other request-level middleware.
Persistence beyond the existing in-memory Map, and any change to id allocation strategy.
toy/README.md, OpenAPI/schema docs, or CHANGELOG updates.
Modifying toy/test/helpers.js, toy/test/health.test.js, or toy/package.json.
risk_reasons: Toy/example application with no production users or persistent data at risk
Narrowly scoped: single validation rule on one endpoint, no schema or infrastructure changes
Does not touch auth, payments, or critical systems
Validation-only change; in-memory storage structure unchanged
Well-defined and explicitly bounded scope with clear out-of-scope items
Easily reversible; not an irreversible data migration or infrastructure change

tasks.description: Implement 64-character length validation in POST /items handler. Add a check that rejects names longer than 64 UTF-16 code units with HTTP 400 and response body { "error": "name too long" }. The length check must run after the existing presence/type check to preserve current error messages for missing/empty/non-string names. Names of exactly 64 characters or fewer must be accepted with the existing 201 create behavior. Do not consume id or mutate state on rejection.

Add comprehensive test cases to toy/test/items.test.js covering all length validation scenarios: 65-character string rejection, 64-character string acceptance, 63-character string acceptance (boundary), unchanged behavior for missing/empty/non-string names, and verification that rejected requests do not consume ids or mutate state. Run the full test suite to verify all pre-existing tests in items.test.js and health.test.js continue to pass.
